# Tool reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_tool_docs.py from the tool definitions. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every tool returns JSON. Dates are US Pacific time; percentages are 0-100. Read-only tools are
annotated `readOnlyHint: true` so clients can auto-approve them.

## Account

### `get_auth_status`

*Auth status* · read-only

Check whether the server is signed in to YouTube, which channel it reads, and which permissions were granted. Call this first if any other tool reports a sign-in problem.

### `authenticate`

*Sign in to YouTube* · has side effects (no channel changes)

Start Google sign-in in the user's browser and return the sign-in URL immediately. The user must approve access in the browser (choosing the account or Brand Account that owns the channel). Afterwards call `get_auth_status` to confirm. Only works when the MCP server runs on the user's own computer. Signing in again replaces the stored token.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `include_revenue` | boolean | `true` | Also request read access to revenue reports (only useful for monetized channels). |
| `include_comments` | boolean | `false` | Also request YouTube's 'manage' permission, which Google requires even to read comments. Only if the user wants the comment tools. |

## Channel & content

### `get_channel`

*Channel overview* · read-only

The signed-in channel's profile and lifetime public stats: subscribers, total views, video count, creation date, country, handle, description, keywords and topics.

### `list_videos`

*List videos* · read-only

List the channel's uploads (including private/unlisted/scheduled, newest first) with public lifetime stats: views, likes, comments, engagement rate, duration, format guess. Costs ~1 quota unit per 50 videos. For period-specific performance use get_top_videos.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | `50` | Maximum videos to return. |
| `sort_by` | `newest` \| `oldest` \| `most_viewed` \| `most_liked` \| `most_commented` \| `highest_engagement` | `"newest"` | Order of the returned videos (sorting happens over the scanned uploads). |
| `published_after` | string \| null | `null` | Only videos published on/after YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `published_before` | string \| null | `null` | Only videos published on/before YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `content_format` | `short` \| `video` \| `live` \| null | `null` | Filter by format using public metadata: 'short' = up to 3 minutes (likely Shorts), 'video' = longer uploads, 'live' = live streams/premieres. |
| `title_contains` | string \| null | `null` | Case-insensitive title filter. |
| `playlist_id` | string \| null | `null` | List this playlist instead of the channel's uploads. |
| `save_to` | string \| null | `null` | Optional file to also save the rows to (.csv or .json). A bare filename goes in the output directory; absolute paths are allowed. |

### `get_videos_details`

*Video details* · read-only

Full metadata and lifetime public stats for specific videos: title, description, tags, category, privacy, duration, captions, live-stream details, views, likes, comments.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `video_ids` | list[string] | **required** | Up to 50 video IDs. |

### `list_playlists`

*List playlists* · read-only

The channel's playlists with item counts and privacy. Use list_videos(playlist_id=...) to see a playlist's videos.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | `50` | Maximum playlists to return. |

### `list_comments`

*List comments* · read-only

Read comment threads (top-level comments with reply counts) for the channel or one video, e.g. to summarise audience sentiment, find questions, or spot content ideas. Requires the optional 'manage' permission (`youtube-studio-mcp auth --comments`): YouTube has no read-only permission for comments.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `video_id` | string \| null | `null` | Comments on one video. Omit for recent comments across the channel. |
| `limit` | integer | `50` | Maximum comment threads to return. |
| `order` | `time` \| `relevance` | `"time"` | Newest first, or YouTube's relevance. |
| `search_terms` | string \| null | `null` | Only threads containing this text. |
| `moderation_status` | `published` \| `heldForReview` \| `likelySpam` | `"published"` | 'heldForReview' / 'likelySpam' show the comments waiting in Studio's review queue. |
| `include_replies` | boolean | `false` | Include up to 5 replies per thread. |
| `save_to` | string \| null | `null` | Optional file to also save the rows to (.csv or .json). A bare filename goes in the output directory; absolute paths are allowed. |

## Analytics

### `get_performance_summary`

*Performance summary* · read-only

Headline numbers for a period, like Studio's Overview tab: views, engaged views, watch time (hours), average view duration/percentage, subscribers gained/lost/net, likes, comments, shares, engagement rate, optionally revenue, each with the previous period and % change. Works for the channel or a single video.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `period` | `last_7_days` \| `last_28_days` \| `last_90_days` \| `last_365_days` \| `this_month` \| `last_month` \| `this_year` \| `last_year` \| `all_time` \| null | `"last_28_days"` | Named date range, Studio-style. Rolling ranges end at the latest complete day of data (analytics lag ~2-3 days; dates are US Pacific). Ignored when start_date is set. |
| `start_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range start, YYYY-MM-DD. Overrides `period`. |
| `end_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range end, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to the latest complete day. |
| `video_id` | string \| null | `null` | Limit to one video (11-character ID, e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ'). Omit for the whole channel. |
| `compare_to_previous` | boolean | `true` | Also fetch the previous period of equal length and compute % change. |
| `include_revenue` | boolean | `false` | Add estimated revenue, RPM, CPM etc. (monetized channels only). |

### `get_metrics_over_time`

*Metrics over time* · read-only

A time series of metrics by day, week, month or year — for trend analysis and growth charts. Adds netSubscribers when gained and lost are both requested. Buckets cut off by the date range are flagged partial=true.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metrics` | list[string] \| null | `null` | Analytics metric names. Default: views, estimatedMinutesWatched, subscribersGained, subscribersLost. Others: engagedViews, likes, comments, shares, averageViewDuration, averageViewPercentage, estimatedRevenue, estimatedAdRevenue, cpm, playbackBasedCpm, ... |
| `granularity` | `day` \| `week` \| `month` \| `year` | `"day"` | Bucket size. Weeks start on Monday. |
| `period` | `last_7_days` \| `last_28_days` \| `last_90_days` \| `last_365_days` \| `this_month` \| `last_month` \| `this_year` \| `last_year` \| `all_time` \| null | `"last_90_days"` | Named date range, Studio-style. Rolling ranges end at the latest complete day of data (analytics lag ~2-3 days; dates are US Pacific). Ignored when start_date is set. |
| `start_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range start, YYYY-MM-DD. Overrides `period`. |
| `end_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range end, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to the latest complete day. |
| `video_id` | string \| null | `null` | Limit to one video (11-character ID, e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ'). Omit for the whole channel. |
| `content_type` | `shorts` \| `videos` \| `live` \| null | `null` | Only Shorts, regular videos, or live streams. |
| `include_cumulative_subscribers` | boolean | `false` | Add totalSubscribers per bucket (running total of net subscribers since the channel started; great for growth charts). Channel-wide only. |
| `save_to` | string \| null | `null` | Optional file to also save the rows to (.csv or .json). A bare filename goes in the output directory; absolute paths are allowed. |

| `period` | `last_7_days` \| `last_28_days` \| `last_90_days` \| `last_365_days` \| `this_month` \| `last_month` \| `this_year` \| `last_year` \| `all_time` \| null | `"last_28_days"` | Named date range, Studio-style. Rolling ranges end at the latest complete day of data (analytics lag ~2-3 days; dates are US Pacific). Ignored when start_date is set. |
| `start_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range start, YYYY-MM-DD. Overrides `period`. |
| `end_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range end, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to the latest complete day. |
| `content_type` | `shorts` \| `videos` \| `live` \| null | `null` | Only rank Shorts, regular videos, or live streams. |
| `save_to` | string \| null | `null` | Optional file to also save the rows to (.csv or .json). A bare filename goes in the output directory; absolute paths are allowed. |

Rolling ranges end at the latest complete day of data (analytics lag ~2-3 days; dates are US Pacific). Ignored when start_date is set. |
| `start_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range start, YYYY-MM-DD. Overrides `period`. |

How viewers find the content: views and watch time by traffic source (search, suggested, browse, Shorts feed, external, ...) or, with source_type, the top search terms / referring videos / websites for that source.

Rolling ranges end at the latest complete day of data (analytics lag ~2-3 days; dates are US Pacific). Ignored when start_date is set. |

### `get_audience_retention`

*Audience retention* · read-only

The audience-retention curve for one video, with timestamps, key retention milestones and the steepest drop-off moments. Defaults to the video's lifetime. audience_watch_ratio = share of viewers still watching at that moment (can exceed 1 when people rewatch a part). relative_retention compares with similar-length YouTube videos (0-1; above 0.5 is better than average).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `video_id` | string | **required** | The video to analyse (one ID). |
| `period` | `last_7_days` \| `last_28_days` \| `last_90_days` \| `last_365_days` \| `this_month` \| `last_month` \| `this_year` \| `last_year` \| `all_time` \| null | `null` | Named date range, Studio-style. Rolling ranges end at the latest complete day of data (analytics lag ~2-3 days; dates are US Pacific). Ignored when start_date is set. |
| `start_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range start, YYYY-MM-DD. Overrides `period`. |
| `end_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range end, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to the latest complete day. |
| `audience_type` | `ORGANIC` \| `AD_INSTREAM` \| `AD_INDISPLAY` \| null | `null` | Only organic views, or views from in-stream / in-feed ads. |
| `subscribed_status` | `SUBSCRIBED` \| `UNSUBSCRIBED` \| null | `null` | Only subscribers or non-subscribers. |
| `points` | integer | `50` | Number of points in the returned curve (down-sampled from 100). |

### `query_analytics`

*Custom analytics query* · read-only

Run any YouTube Analytics API v2 report for the channel (ids=channel==MINE) — the escape hatch when no other tool fits. See https://developers.google.com/youtube/analytics/channel_reports for valid combinations. Notes: the 'video' dimension needs sort and max_results <= 200; 'insightTrafficSourceDetail' needs a filter on insightTrafficSourceType, sort and max_results <= 25; demographics (ageGroup/gender) only support viewerPercentage; the 'month' dimension aligns dates to whole months automatically. YouTube's error message is returned if a combination is invalid.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metrics` | list[string] | **required** | Metric API names, e.g. ['views', 'likes']. |
| `dimensions` | list[string] \| null | `null` | Dimension API names, e.g. ['day'], ['video'], ['country', 'creatorContentType']. |
| `filters` | string \| null | `null` | Analytics filter string, e.g. 'video==ID1,ID2;country==US' (';' = AND). |
| `sort` | string \| null | `null` | Comma-separated sort, '-' for descending, e.g. '-views'. |
| `max_results` | integer \| null | `null` | Row limit. |
| `period` | `last_7_days` \| `last_28_days` \| `last_90_days` \| `last_365_days` \| `this_month` \| `last_month` \| `this_year` \| `last_year` \| `all_time` \| null | `"last_28_days"` | Named date range, Studio-style. Rolling ranges end at the latest complete day of data (analytics lag ~2-3 days; dates are US Pacific). Ignored when start_date is set. |
| `start_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range start, YYYY-MM-DD. Overrides `period`. |
| `end_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range end, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to the latest complete day. |
| `currency` | string \| null | `null` | Currency for revenue metrics (ISO 4217). |
| `save_to` | string \| null | `null` | Optional file to also save the rows to (.csv or .json). A bare filename goes in the output directory; absolute paths are allowed. |

## Impressions & CTR (beta)

### `enable_impressions_reports`

*Enable impressions reports* · has side effects (no channel changes)

One-time setup for thumbnail impressions & click-through rate (CTR), which the Analytics API does not provide. Creates a YouTube Reporting API job for the channel (safe to call again). YouTube then publishes daily reports: the first ones ~48 hours later, plus 30 days of history. Use get_impressions afterwards.

### `get_impressions`

*Impressions & CTR (beta)* · read-only

Thumbnail impressions and impressions click-through rate (CTR) from the YouTube Reporting API, by day, by video, or in total. Requires enable_impressions_reports to have been run at least ~2 days earlier; only days YouTube has published are included.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group_by` | `day` \| `video` \| `total` | `"total"` | Daily trend, per-video ranking, or one total for the period. |
| `period` | `last_7_days` \| `last_28_days` \| `last_90_days` \| `last_365_days` \| `this_month` \| `last_month` \| `this_year` \| `last_year` \| `all_time` \| null | `"last_28_days"` | Named date range, Studio-style. Rolling ranges end at the latest complete day of data (analytics lag ~2-3 days; dates are US Pacific). Ignored when start_date is set. |
| `start_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range start, YYYY-MM-DD. Overrides `period`. |
| `end_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range end, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to the latest complete day. |
| `limit` | integer | `25` | Maximum rows for group_by='video'. |

## Media kit & charts

### `get_media_kit_data`

*Media kit data* · read-only

Everything a creator media kit / sponsor deck needs, as one stable JSON snapshot (schema_version 1, snake_case, *_pct 0-100, *_s seconds): channel profile, period performance vs previous period, Shorts vs long-form performance, impressions funnel, daily and monthly trends, audience age/gender/countries/devices, recent uploads with thumbnails, top videos and traffic sources. Anything YouTube can't provide is null and explained in `unavailable` instead of failing the call.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `period` | `last_7_days` \| `last_28_days` \| `last_90_days` \| `last_365_days` \| `this_month` \| `last_month` \| `this_year` \| `last_year` \| `all_time` \| null | `"last_28_days"` | Named date range, Studio-style. Rolling ranges end at the latest complete day of data (analytics lag ~2-3 days; dates are US Pacific). Ignored when start_date is set. |
| `start_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range start, YYYY-MM-DD. Overrides `period`. |
| `end_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range end, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to the latest complete day. |
| `trend_months` | integer | `12` | Months in monthly_trend. |
| `recent_uploads` | integer | `10` | Recent long-form videos and Shorts to list and average (each). |
| `min_upload_age_days` | integer | `7` | Skip uploads younger than this (their views are still growing). |
| `top_countries` | integer | `8` | Countries to include. |
| `include_revenue` | boolean | `false` | Add revenue/RPM to performance (most media kits don't show it). |
| `save_to` | string \| null | `null` | Also save the snapshot as JSON (bare filename -> output directory). |

### `create_chart`

*Create chart* · has side effects (no channel changes)

Render a polished, media-kit-ready chart (PNG, SVG or PDF) from data you provide — typically numbers from the analytics tools. Uses a colour-blind-safe palette by default, thin marks, clean axes and direct value labels. Returns the saved file path(s) and a preview image.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chart_type` | `line` \| `area` \| `bar` \| `horizontal_bar` \| `stacked_bar` \| `donut` | **required** | line/area: trends over time. bar: compare categories (multiple series = grouped). horizontal_bar: ranked lists with long labels (countries, videos, traffic sources). stacked_bar: parts of a total per category. donut: share of one whole (max 6 slices). |
| `labels` | list[string] | **required** | X-axis categories or dates. ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM, YYYY) get smart date ticks. |
| `series` | list[SeriesInput] | **required** | 1-8 data series. |
| `title` | string | **required** | Chart title (the headline). |
| `subtitle` | string \| null | `null` | Smaller line under the title, e.g. the period. |
| `source_note` | string \| null | `null` | Footnote, e.g. 'Source: YouTube Analytics, Aug–Oct 2026'. |
| `x_label` | string \| null | `null` |  |
| `y_label` | string \| null | `null` |  |
| `value_format` | `auto` \| `number` \| `compact` \| `percent` \| `duration` \| `currency` | `"auto"` | How numbers print: compact (12.3K), percent (values already 0-100), duration (values in seconds -> m:ss), currency, number, or auto. |
| `currency_symbol` | string | `"$"` |  |
| `colors` | list[string] \| null | `null` | Brand colours as hex, used in order for series (or donut slices). |
| `highlight` | string \| null | `null` | For a single-series bar chart: the label to emphasise; other bars are muted. |
| `theme` | `light` \| `dark` | `"light"` | Light or dark background. |
| `transparent_background` | boolean | `false` | Transparent PNG/SVG background for placing on designed pages. |
| `width` | integer | `1600` | Width in pixels. |
| `height` | integer | `900` | Height in pixels. |
| `show_values` | `auto` \| `none` \| `all` \| `last` | `"auto"` | Value labels: auto (bars when few, line end points), all, last, or none. |
| `font_family` | string \| null | `null` | Installed font name, e.g. 'Montserrat'. Falls back if missing. |
| `y_min` | number \| null | `null` | Force the value-axis minimum. |
| `y_max` | number \| null | `null` | Force the value-axis maximum. |
| `filename` | string \| null | `null` | Where to save. Bare names go to the output directory; absolute paths allowed. The extension (.png/.svg/.pdf) picks the format. Default: <title>-<timestamp>.png. |
| `extra_formats` | list[`png` \| `svg` \| `pdf`] \| null | `null` | Also save these formats next to the main file, e.g. ['svg'] for print. |
| `include_preview` | boolean | `true` | Return a small PNG preview so you can check the chart visually. |

## Write tools (opt-in)

### `update_video_details`

*Update video details* · **changes your channel** (opt-in)

Edit a video's title, description, tags, category or visibility. Fields you omit are kept as they are. Defaults to dry_run=true: confirm the shown diff with the user, then call again with dry_run=false. Costs 50 quota units when saving.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `video_id` | string | **required** | The video to edit. |
| `title` | string \| null | `null` | New title (max 100 characters). |
| `description` | string \| null | `null` | New full description (replaces the old one). |
| `tags` | list[string] \| null | `null` | New full tag list (replaces the old one). |
| `category_id` | string \| null | `null` | YouTube category ID, e.g. '22' (People & Blogs). |
| `privacy_status` | `public` \| `unlisted` \| `private` \| null | `null` | Change visibility. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | `true` | Preview the change without saving. Recommended first; show the user the diff. |

### `reply_to_comment`

*Reply to comment* · **changes your channel** (opt-in)

Post a public reply as the channel. Always show the user the exact text and get their approval first. Costs 50 quota units.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `comment_id` | string | **required** | ID of the top-level comment to reply to. |
| `text` | string | **required** | Reply text, posted as the channel. |

### `moderate_comments`

*Moderate comments* · **changes your channel** (opt-in)

Approve, hold or reject comments (like Studio's comment moderation). Confirm with the user before rejecting. Costs 50 quota units.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `comment_ids` | list[string] | **required** | Up to 50 comment IDs. |
| `status` | `published` \| `heldForReview` \| `rejected` | **required** | published = approve, heldForReview = hold, rejected = hide (cannot be undone). |
| `ban_author` | boolean | `false` | With 'rejected': also hide future comments from these authors. |
